text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
- Poland's and Denmark's prime ministers Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz and Poul Nyrup Rasmussen signed a cooperation agreement envisaging free consulting, technological and training assistance by Denmark.

- Around 100 million zlotys from Poland's housing industry fund (KFM) will be spent on housing development in Katowice province, southern Poland, which will allow to build 4,000 new flats in the province, the state-owned Bank Gospodarstwa Krajowego ( BGK) said.
- The EU's PHARE fund has granted 12.3 million European Currency Units (ECU) to the Central Statistical Office (GUS) for the Polstat statistical information system develoment.

- The French-British GEC Alsthom concern has bought the Chorzow-based Konstal rolling stock maker from the National Investment Fund (NFI) No.10. GEC Alsthom will carry an investment programme to improve Konstal's competitiveness and work conditions, the contract said.
- Diego Avesani has recently been replaced by Massimo Gentilini as Fiat Auto Poland's president, the company said.

- Era GSM and Plus GSM digital mobile phone operators want the telecommunications ministry to introduce new, lower rates for services of Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA), the state-owned telecom monopolist, to the mobile phone operators. The present excessive rates block the telecoms development, the companies said.
- Around 50 percent of Poles earning high incomes prefer to low-risk, low-return investments to higher-yielding but more risky ones, a recent survey by the BPS Consulting firm said.

- The Warsaw-based Bank Ochrony Srodowiska (BOS) environmental protection bank has bought a 16 percent stake in the Elektromontaz Poludnie construction firm from the listed Rafako boiler maker, the bank's deputy president Jerzy Pietrewicz said.
- Plus GSM mobile phone operator awarded U.S.'s Lucent Technologies a contract for radio transmission facility delivery worth $20 million.
- Poland expects to receive aid reaching two billion European Currency Units (ECU) every year following accession to the European Union, the government's European Integration Committee said.

- The recently launched Fakty weekly has already spent around two million zlotys on advertising in the last two weeks. Independent media heavily criticise the government's publishing venture, which was funded with taxpayers' money.
- TPSA, the state-owned telecom monopolist, earned a net profit of 850 million zlotys in 1996, which showed a significant decline compared with 933 million zlotys it earned the year before.
